prompt: Instead of SSHing in to patch servers, the team builds a new image and replaces them.
tells: builds a new image and replaces them
why: Replace, don't modify: that's immutable infrastructure.
trap: IaC defines it; the clue is replacing servers.

prompt: One old server behaves differently because of years of hand-made changes.
why: Mutable servers drift into snowflakes. Immutable images prevent it.
trap: It's drift on the machine, not in config values.

prompt: Each release is a container image tagged with the commit; running containers are never changed.
why: Never-changed, versioned images are immutable infrastructure.
trap: Config may still vary, but the image doesn't.

prompt: A broken instance is terminated and a fresh one launched, rather than debugged in place.
why: Treating servers as replaceable is immutable thinking.
trap: Health checks may detect it; the response is replacement.

prompt: A security patch went out by rebuilding the base image and redeploying everything.
why: Patches arrive through new images, not in-place updates.
trap: IaC isn't the clue; the rebuild is.

prompt: Containers run with a read-only filesystem so nobody can change them at runtime.
why: Enforcing no runtime changes supports immutability.
trap: It restricts the app, but the aim is immutability.
